stem: Root-zone EC is much higher in the driest part of a container than in wetter sampled areas. What does this illustrate?
choices: Water distribution can create spatial solute-concentration gradients, so one sample may not represent the entire root zone
EC must be uniform within every container
Only input solution determines local EC
rationale: As water content and movement vary spatially, dissolved salts can concentrate differently within the root zone. Sampling location therefore matters.
